newsitem.title: USA: U.S. retailers report mixed sales for March.
newsitem.headline: U.S. retailers report mixed sales for March.

text.p: U.S. retailers, as expected, reported mixed results for March, with discounters showing the best same-store sales gains for the month while traditional department stores did not perform as well.
Overall, same-store sales were up about five percent or slightly higher, estimated Michael Niemira, analyst with Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd.

"It's a mixed bag," Niemira said, referring to results among discount retailers and traditional department stores. He added some advance sales in February, particularly for apparel, may have stolen some sales from March.
Standard & Poor's Equity Group analyst Karen Sack said discount-department stores performed the best in March, while apparel and fashion merchandisers may have seen some sales deferred until April.
Kmart Corp said its March same-store sales, on a consolidated basis, rose 12.7 percent, and U.S. Kmart same-store sales were up 13 percent. Kmart shares were up 3/8 at 12-7/8.
Wal-Mart Stores Inc reported a 7.2 percent rise in March same-store sales. Wal-Mart shares were off 1/4 at 28-3/8.
Sears, Roebuck and Co shares fell 1-7/8 to 49 after that retailer reported a one percent increase in March same store sales, which analysts said was below expectations.
Separately, Sears also filed a plan to repay certain credit card debtors, who have previously filed for bankruptcy. Sears said that plan could have a material effect on 1997 annual earnings.
